text: Now last night, afore I went to bed, I only had a scantling o’ cheese and—” “I don’t want to hear it!” roared Henchard. “To-morrow the waggons must start at four, and if you’re not here, stand clear. I’ll mortify thy flesh for thee!” “But let me clear up my points, your worshipful——” Henchard turned away. “He asked me and he questioned me, and then ’a wouldn’t hear my points!” said Abel, to the yard in general. “Now, I shall twitch like a moment-hand all night to-night for fear o’ him!” The journey to be taken by the waggons next day was a long one into Blackmoor Vale, and at four o’clock lanterns were moving about the yard.
